description: A safety officer must decide how to contain a solvent leak in a paint booth and authorize the recovery plan for affected production, with input from maintenance, environmental compliance, production supervision, and quality.

shared_context.S1: Paint Booth 4 was stopped this morning after solvent was found pooled beneath its circulation manifold.
shared_context.S2: Elena makes the final decision on containment, restart authorization, and the recovery plan.
shared_context.S3: The booth is currently isolated from production, and the spill area has been cordoned off.
shared_context.S4: The incident authorization form requires documented entries for equipment repair, hazardous-waste handling, production recovery, and disposition of potentially contaminated panels before Booth 4 can be restarted.
shared_context.S5: Booth 4's restart authorization policy requires findings from maintenance, environmental compliance, production, and quality to be attached to the incident form before the authorization can be finalized.

PF1.text: Victor's inspection found a cracked manifold isolation valve seat. Replacing the valve requires exactly 4 hours, and maintenance's lockout worksheet identifies exactly 6 isolation points; he completed the inspection this morning but has not attached the worksheet to the incident record. Because the valve seat is cracked, Booth 4 must not be authorized to restart regardless of whether the documentation entries are later completed.

PF2.text: Nadia's measured cleanup estimate is exactly 240 liters of solvent-contaminated liquid. Because the liquid exceeds the plant's hazardous-waste threshold, it requires a licensed hauler and a hazardous-waste manifest; she confirmed the threshold with the waste contractor today but has not entered the estimate in the waste log.

PF3.text: Owen confirmed that Booth 2 can run exactly 180 affected units per shift on both Wednesday and Thursday, allowing exactly 360 units from the Booth 4 schedule to be rerouted there without exceeding its approved rate; he received the capacity confirmation from the scheduling desk but has not revised the production board.

PF4.text: Priya's wipe sampling found solvent residue on exactly 36 panels that were staged beside Booth 4. Those panels must remain on quality hold and receive solvent-residue inspection before release; she completed the sampling this morning but has not issued the hold tags.

acceptance_conditions: Booth 4 must remain unauthorized to restart because of the cracked valve seat.
The repair plan must reserve exactly 4 hours of downtime.
Exactly 6 lockout isolation points must be verified.
Exactly 360 units must be rerouted to Booth 2.
Exactly 36 panels must be held for solvent-residue inspection.
Exactly 240 liters of contaminated liquid must be identified for licensed hazardous-waste handling.
A documentation commitment must be recorded for the hazardous-waste handling requirement.
The valve-seat finding must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C7: decisions['hazardous_waste_volume_liters'] == 240 and any(c['type'] == 'documentation' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The cracked valve seat changes restart authorization to false regardless of documentation, sets repair downtime to exactly 4 hours, and changes lockout verification to exactly 6 isolation points.
The measured contamination changes the waste entry to exactly 240 liters and requires a documentation commitment for licensed hazardous-waste handling.
The confirmed Booth 2 capacity changes the recovery allocation to exactly 360 units rerouted to Booth 2.
The wipe-sampling result changes the disposition to exactly 36 panels held with mandatory solvent-residue inspection.
